method.summary: Summary of every driver's race: start, finish, stops and pace consistency.
steps: Start position = a driver's first recorded position sample; finish position = the last sample.
Stops = number of tyre stints - 1.
Best / median / std lap use the CLEAN laps (steps below).
Start from every lap that passed validation (physically plausible duration, valid numbers).
Remove laps with no recorded duration.
Remove out-laps (first lap after leaving the pits - cold tyres, pit-lane exit).
Remove laps that overlap a safety car, virtual safety car or red-flag period (taken from race-control messages; see limitations).
Compute the adjusted time = lap time + 0.03 s x lap number (adds back the time gained as the car burns fuel).
Remove laps whose adjusted time is more than 1.07x that driver's median adjusted time (in-laps, traffic, incidents). The median uses laps that survived the previous steps.
method.formula: positions gained = start position - finish position;  lap_std = standard deviation of clean lap times
method.baseline: Each driver against their own laps; no cross-driver baseline.
limitations: OpenF1 does not provide the official classification here, so 'finish position' is the last live position sample and can differ from the official result (penalties, DSQ).

Safety-car periods are detected from the wording of race-control messages (DEPLOYED ... ENDING / IN THIS LAP, red flag ... clear/green). If the wording changes or messages are missing, those laps are only caught by the slow-lap rule.

method.summary: Race position of every driver at the start of each lap.
steps: For each lap, take the position sample closest in time to the lap start timestamp.
method.formula: position(driver, lap) = nearest position sample to lap.date_start
limitations: Nearest-sample matching: a position change inside a lap shows up on the next lap.

method.summary: Clean lap times of every driver.
steps: Start from every lap that passed validation (physically plausible duration, valid numbers).
Remove laps with no recorded duration.
Remove out-laps (first lap after leaving the pits - cold tyres, pit-lane exit).
Remove laps that overlap a safety car, virtual safety car or red-flag period (taken from race-control messages; see limitations).
Compute the adjusted time = lap time + 0.03 s x lap number (adds back the time gained as the car burns fuel).
Remove laps whose adjusted time is more than 1.07x that driver's median adjusted time (in-laps, traffic, incidents). The median uses laps that survived the previous steps.
method.formula: plotted value = the real lap time (seconds), not the fuel-adjusted one
assumptions: The fuel correction of 0.03 s per lap is an assumption, not a measurement; the true value varies by circuit and car.
limitations: Safety-car periods are detected from the wording of race-control messages (DEPLOYED ... ENDING / IN THIS LAP, red flag ... clear/green). If the wording changes or messages are missing, those laps are only caught by the slow-lap rule.

method.summary: Each driver's tyre stints: compound and lap range.
steps: Each stint becomes one bar from lap_start-1 to lap_end.
limitations: If a stint has no recorded end the API's lap_end is used as given.

steps: Remove stops with a pit-lane time >= 40.0 s (repairs / red-flag stops that say nothing about normal stop speed).
method.formula: plotted value = pit-lane time (entry to exit), seconds
limitations: This is time in the pit lane, not the total race time lost by stopping.

method.summary: How much slower the car gets as the tyres age, per compound.
steps: Start from every lap that passed validation (physically plausible duration, valid numbers).
Remove laps with no recorded duration.
Remove out-laps (first lap after leaving the pits - cold tyres, pit-lane exit).
Remove laps that overlap a safety car, virtual safety car or red-flag period (taken from race-control messages; see limitations).
Compute the adjusted time = lap time + 0.03 s x lap number (adds back the time gained as the car burns fuel).
Remove laps whose adjusted time is more than 1.07x that driver's median adjusted time (in-laps, traffic, incidents). The median uses laps that survived the previous steps.
Attach compound and tyre age: age = age at stint start + lap - stint start lap + 1.
Keep ages up to 35.
delta = adjusted lap time - driver's median adjusted time (so +0.5 means 0.5 s slower than the driver's typical pace).
Average delta per (compound, age); keep a point only if it has >= 3 laps in a race (15 when pooling races); keep a compound only with >= 4 ages.
assumptions: The fuel correction of 0.03 s per lap is an assumption, not a measurement; the true value varies by circuit and car.
limitations: Tyre age and track evolution overlap: the track gets faster over a race, which flatters old tyres.

method.summary: Track and air temperature during the session.
steps: No filtering beyond validation.
limitations: Weather is sampled about once a minute at one point of the circuit.

charts.title: Pace vs field and vs teammate

method.summary: A driver's clean lap time compared with the whole field and with their teammate, lap by lap.
steps: Start from every lap that passed validation (physically plausible duration, valid numbers).
Remove laps with no recorded duration.
Remove out-laps (first lap after leaving the pits - cold tyres, pit-lane exit).
Remove laps that overlap a safety car, virtual safety car or red-flag period (taken from race-control messages; see limitations).
Compute the adjusted time = lap time + 0.03 s x lap number (adds back the time gained as the car burns fuel).
Remove laps whose adjusted time is more than 1.07x that driver's median adjusted time (in-laps, traffic, incidents). The median uses laps that survived the previous steps.
delta vs field = adjusted time - median adjusted time of ALL drivers' clean laps in the race.
delta vs teammate = adjusted time - teammate's adjusted time on the same lap (needs both clean).
method.formula: delta_field = adj - median(adj, all clean laps);  delta_teammate = adj - adj_teammate(lap)
method.baseline: Field median of the race / the teammate's same-lap time. Negative = faster.
assumptions: The fuel correction of 0.03 s per lap is an assumption, not a measurement; the true value varies by circuit and car.
limitations: Field median mixes different tyre ages and fuel loads; use it as a rough guide.

method.summary: Every lap of the driver, including the ones removed from the analysis.
steps: No lap is hidden: the 'status' column says 'clean' or the rule that removed the lap.
method.formula: status = clean or the id of the first cleaning rule the lap failed
limitations: Safety-car periods are detected from the wording of race-control messages (DEPLOYED ... ENDING / IN THIS LAP, red flag ... clear/green). If the wording changes or messages are missing, those laps are only caught by the slow-lap rule.

steps: Start from every lap that passed validation (physically plausible duration, valid numbers).
Remove laps with no recorded duration.
Remove out-laps (first lap after leaving the pits - cold tyres, pit-lane exit).
Remove laps that overlap a safety car, virtual safety car or red-flag period (taken from race-control messages; see limitations).
Compute the adjusted time = lap time + 0.03 s x lap number (adds back the time gained as the car burns fuel).
Remove laps whose adjusted time is more than 1.07x that driver's median adjusted time (in-laps, traffic, incidents). The median uses laps that survived the previous steps.
avg pace = mean clean lap time inside the stint.
deg per lap = slope of a straight line fitted to (tyre age, adjusted time); only for stints with >= 5 clean laps.
method.formula: deg_per_lap = slope of least-squares fit  adj_time ~ tyre_age
assumptions: The fuel correction of 0.03 s per lap is an assumption, not a measurement; the true value varies by circuit and car.
limitations: Straight-line fit; real degradation is often non-linear (a 'cliff').

method.summary: Car positions on a circuit drawing, scrubbable through the race.
steps: Location samples were downsampled when loaded: one per driver every 2.0 s.
Samples with x = y = z = 0 (invalid frames) are removed.

All drivers are put on one shared clock (seconds since session start) by linear interpolation. Before a driver's first and after their last sample (e.g. a retirement) the dot is simply not drawn; gaps in the middle are bridged by the interpolation.
The circuit outline is one driver's clean lap drawn through its location samples.
The running order comes from the position table, NOT from where the dots are on the drawing.
method.formula: x(t), y(t) = linear interpolation between the two nearest samples of that driver
limitations: Coarse sampling makes the outline polygonal and can cut corners.
Location data may be missing for some races; the map is then unavailable.
'Received' location rows are counted after downsampling.
